subject.title: Culver City Unified School District Board

text: Age: 54
Occupation: Parent/Attorney

As a proud CCUSD parent of two and a Culver City resident for 20 years, I'm passionate about improving the quality and reputation of Culver City schools. After earning degrees from UC San Diego, Stanford Law School, and UCLA, I began my career as a lawyer. Today, I'm the Culver City Downtown Business Association Executive Director, where I created High School Senior Day, inviting local businesses to celebrate our graduates. I also chair the Culver City Planning Commission and serve on the Measure E Bond Oversight Committee.
CCUSD is a $100 million operation serving over 6,000 students and 700 teachers and staff. Running it well takes serious focus on budgets and academics.
I'm endorsed by Teachers, School Board members, City Council members, and local parents.
I would be honored to earn your vote.
Learn more: www.mentheforculvercity.com

text: I am committed to ensuring every student receives a high-quality public education in an inclusive school environment. As CCUSD's board president, I lead with collaboration, transparency, and fiscal responsibility to strengthen our schools and expand opportunities for every student. Stewarding over $300 million in annual investments throughout my professional career, I have the experience to safeguard our district's financial health. I will continue building trust in our district through open communication, accountability, and engagement with the community.

BACKGROUND
- Culver City Unified School District Board President
- Vice-Chair Membership/Outreach, Filipino American Democratic Caucus of California Democratic Party
- Media and Marketing Executive

ACCOMPLISHMENTS
- Advanced Culver City's reputation as a destination district
- Expanded student wellness and learning opportunities
- Renewed funding to protect teacher salaries
- Improved the district's long-term fiscal stability
- Strengthened partnerships with Culver City government

COMMITMENTS
- Achievement: empower students to thrive through equity, support, and opportunity
- Belonging: ensure safe, inclusive schools where every student is respected and supported
- Community: build sustainable environments where students, educators, and families can thrive

ENDORSEMENTS
Culver City Federation of Teachers, Culver City Democratic Club, Asian Democrats of LA County, Pilipino LA Democrats, Stonewall Democratic Club Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi; Senator Lola Smallwood-Cuevas; LA County Assessor Jeff Prang; Culver City Mayor Freddy Puza and Vice Mayor Bubba Fish; CCUSD Board Members Triston Ezidore, Brian Guerrero, and Andrew Lachman; LA City Controller Kenneth Mejia; LA City Councilmember Ysabel Jurado
www.StephanieLoredo.com

text: Occupation: School Board Member/Clean Energy Manager
Four years ago, you elected me to bring bold, student-centered leadership to Culver City schools. Since then, I've worked every day to deliver on that promise.

- Raised graduation rates to 97%
- Passed Measure E, investing $358 million to modernize our schools
- Made historic investments in arts education and career pathways
- Balanced our budget while protecting investments in students and classrooms
- Established a Black Student Achievement goal to close persistent opportunity gaps
- Secured millions in additional City funding for our schools
- Advanced our Student Green New Deal and sustainability initiatives
- Championed stronger mental health supports and safe, welcoming schools
- Secured good-paying union jobs as we rebuild our campuses

There is more work ahead. In my next term, I'll focus on improving math and literacy, retaining exceptional educators, strengthening student mental health, and expanding arts and career opportunities.
I'm proud of our progress and ask for your vote to continue building excellent schools where every student can thrive.

- Senator Adam Schiff, Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove, State Superintendent Tony Thurmond, Mayor Freddy Puza
- Dolores Huerta
- Sierra Club
- Community leaders across Culver City
www.tristonezidore.com

text: As a parent, educator, union organizer and policy analyst, I've brought my unique set of skills to the Culver City Unified School Board for the last 4 years, and, as the only teacher and union member on the Board, I've driven policies that have moved CCUSD forward and resulted in positive outcomes for students.

When I ran 4 years ago, I promised to work with teachers, classified staff, students and families to:
1. Provide high-quality academic, social-emotional, artistic and athletic experiences for all students on safe, well-maintained campuses.
2. Improve access and inclusion, particularly students with disabilities and English learners.
3. Examine existing policies and practices for barriers to student success, asking difficult questions, using data, and listening to the experiences of students and families.
4. Value diversity and engage with different communities on matters that impact students, families, and employees.

I have delivered on those promises, and we've made steady progress... but we still have work to do. I believe we need to continue forward, focusing on student opportunities and outcomes, working with our labor partners, and building the confidence of the community until we've revitalized CCUSD and made it the pride of our community.
Visit my website: http://www.brianguerrero4ccusd.com
